assessments.criteria: Documents parse without unaddressed errors that affect meaning; language, title, headings, landmarks, unique identifiers, links, meaningful alternative text, table headings/caption, and source order match the stated information relationships. The learner distinguishes informative from decorative imagery, traces navigation and fragment targets, and explains any remaining browser-repair behavior.
assessments.evidence: Complete local HTML files and assets; a page/link map; validator findings with corrections; before/after source and DOM excerpts; keyboard navigation observations and a short rationale for semantics.
assessments.work: Create two linked, independently intelligible HTML documents for a realistic public-information task. One must include a nested content hierarchy, a navigation landmark, an informative figure, and a genuinely tabular dataset with suitable table semantics. Inspect both source and parsed DOM, document at least two deliberate semantic corrections, and demonstrate that links and fragments work without scripting.

assessments.criteria: Every relevant control has an accessible name and meaningful input purpose; grouped choices use suitable semantics; native validation distinguishes missing, malformed, and valid states where applicable; focus is visible; keyboard navigation is logical; user data is not silently sent to an outside endpoint. The learner correctly identifies the limits of native client-side validation and avoids claiming backend security.
assessments.evidence: HTML form, synthetic test matrix, inspection of labels/relationships, keyboard/focus observations, documented invalid and corrected inputs, and explanation of local-only handling and its limitations.
assessments.work: Author a static contact or request form with text, one grouped choice, contextual help, and at least two meaningful native validation constraints. Demonstrate a valid-input path and invalid-input variants with fabricated data; explain submission semantics and why a static-only page does not persist or process input. Perform a keyboard-only review including label activation, focus indication, required-state and error recovery.

assessments.criteria: Predictions match browser computed styles with correct reasoning about origin, importance, layer precedence, specificity, inheritance, and source order; visual hierarchy remains readable; box and layout decisions respond to content rather than fixed pixels; Flexbox and Grid are used for their appropriate layout axes; the injected defect has a reproducible root cause and regression check; reuse does not create unexplainable overrides.
assessments.evidence: HTML/CSS source, a concise prediction-versus-observation matrix covering each named cascade mechanism, DevTools computed-style notes, wide/narrow comparison, injected-failure reproduction and repair, and concise rationale for the refactor.
assessments.work: Implement a small responsive article-and-cards interface using a reusable visual token set and both Flexbox and Grid where each is justified. Predict and then inspect conflicting CSS declarations that together exercise user-agent versus author origins, importance, cascade layers, specificity, inheritance, and source order. Introduce an overflow or alignment defect and repair it without an indiscriminate `!important` override. Refactor one repeated style pattern and verify the result.

assessments.criteria: Ordinary content and controls remain operable and understandable at constrained sizes without unintended horizontal page scrolling; focus is visible and not completely obscured by authored elements; tested color combinations meet stated contrast thresholds (normal text 4.5:1 and large text 3:1 where WCAG 2.2 AA applies); images have appropriate alternatives or decorative treatment and do not cause avoidable layout jumps; relevant fallback content remains usable. These checks do not assert full WCAG conformance.
assessments.evidence: Browser/viewport/zoom test log with limitations, keyboard focus sequence, contrast calculations, image inspection/waterfall or equivalent local observation, source and repaired states, and a cross-browser or supplied-support-case explanation.
assessments.work: Extend an interface with responsive media and a resource-aware content layout. Test at narrow and wide CSS viewports, at 200% browser zoom, and with keyboard navigation; assess representative contrast and focus visibility, form or navigation usability, image alternatives, image dimensions and one loading-related trade-off. Exercise a supported and a fallback CSS behavior without relying on JavaScript.

assessments.criteria: The complete site is reproducible with freely available local tooling, usable without JavaScript, backed by appropriate semantic structure, and navigable by keyboard. Required pages, links, forms, assets, responsive states, and documented acceptance tests work as claimed. Blockers to essential keyboard navigation, understandable content and form use, focus visibility, and required contrast or responsive usability must be corrected before a passing decision; disclosing such a blocker does not satisfy the criterion. Other unresolved limitations must be recorded and their impact bounded. The defense ties concrete implementation and debugging evidence to decisions and avoids claiming untested accessibility or cross-browser guarantees.
assessments.evidence: Repository or portable source archive, README with clean-start commands, page and asset inventory, requirement-to-test matrix, representative keyboard/zoom/viewport and invalid-input checks, validation/diagnostic records, an injected failure and repair, version/environment notes, and a reviewable technical defense.
assessments.work: Deliver a cohesive, at-least-three-page static information site for an explicitly defined audience. Include a structured content page, a meaningful native form demonstration, and reusable responsive layouts; provide linked navigation, local assets, a stylesheet organization strategy, and tested failure states. Conduct a clean-checkout reproduction and defend selected trade-offs in a reviewable written or recorded explanation.

lessons.title: **Course Orientation** — Introduce the course's purpose, the history and evolution of HTML/CSS, common applications, prerequisites, and what this course does not teach.
**The Authoring Loop** — Create, serve on loopback, inspect, and modify a tiny document with freely available tools.
**HTML Document Skeleton** — Construct doctype, html, head, body, language, encoding, and viewport metadata; explain their roles.
**HTML Parsing and the DOM** — Compare source markup, the parsed DOM, and a rendered view; recognize implicit element repair.
**Text and Document Hierarchy** — Build a coherent page outline using headings, paragraphs, emphasis, quotations, and lists.
**Source Validation** — Identify invalid nesting, duplicate identifiers, missing metadata, and repair effects using validation and DOM inspection.

modules.title: From Web Documents to Authored Interfaces

lessons.title: **Page Landmarks** — Distinguish header, main, nav, article, section, aside, and footer through content purpose.
**Navigation Architecture** — Build consistent local and cross-page navigation with understandable link text.
**URLs and Link Safety** — Use relative references, fragments, external destinations, and safe new-window disclosure deliberately.
**Figures and Alternatives** — Choose informative, decorative, and complex-image text alternatives and captions for their actual purpose.
**Data Versus Layout Tables** — Represent genuinely tabular relationships with headers, scope, and captions instead of using tables for layout.
**Media and Embedded Content** — Provide meaningful fallback or captions for local media and explain when an embed creates a privacy boundary.
**Semantics Inspection** — Compare visual grouping with programmatic names, roles, and relationships in developer tools.
**How Native Forms Work** — Distinguish controls, labels, names, values, submission methods, and what a static demonstration can verify.
**Text and Choice Controls** — Select fitting text, email, number, checkbox, radio, select, and textarea semantics for a stated requirement.
**Labels and Help** — Associate explicit labels, fieldsets, legends, hints, and required-state descriptions without placeholder-only labeling.
**Native Constraints** — Apply suitable required, length, type, range, and pattern constraints and inspect browser validity behavior.
**Error and Success Boundaries** — Distinguish built-in client-side feedback from nonexistent server processing and provide readable correction guidance.
**Keyboard Form Journey** — Complete and repair a form using only a keyboard with understandable order and visible focus.
**Privacy-Safe Test Fixtures** — Use fabricated input and local-only demonstrations; avoid collecting or transmitting real personal data.
**CSS Rules and Selectors** — Write type, class, attribute, combinator, and state selectors while minimizing unintentional matches.
**The Cascade Algorithm** — Predict winning declarations from relevance, origin, importance, layers, specificity, scoping proximity, and order.
**Inheritance and Initial Values** — Explain inherited versus noninherited properties and the effects of initial, inherit, unset, and revert.
**Specificity and Layers** — Refactor competing rules with low-specificity selectors and predictable cascade layers.
**Custom Properties** — Use named tokens, fallback expressions, and inheritance to manage a coherent visual system.
**Pseudo-Classes and States** — Style focus, focus-visible, hover, active, invalid, and disabled states without removing usable defaults.
**Computed-Style Diagnosis** — Inspect a contradictory stylesheet and show precisely why a declaration wins or is ignored.

modules.title: The CSS Cascade and Computed Styles

lessons.title: **Typography and Reading** — Choose font stacks, relative sizes, line height, readable line length, and robust text alignment.
**Color and Meaning** — Establish usable contrast and ensure status and emphasis are not communicated by color alone.
**The CSS Box Model** — Predict content, padding, border, and margin dimensions with appropriate box sizing.
**Flow and Spacing** — Use normal flow, block/inline formatting, spacing relationships, and logical direction-aware properties.
**Sizing and Overflow** — Apply min/max constraints, intrinsic sizes, overflow behavior, and sensible long-word wrapping.
**Visual Tokens** — Establish reusable spacing, typography, color, and surface variables without concealing semantics.
**User Text Preferences** — Test text enlargement, zoom, and high-contrast settings for reading and navigation failures.
**Intrinsic Layout First** — Use normal flow and content-based sizing before introducing explicit layout constraints.
**Flexbox Axes and Distribution** — Build one-dimensional navigation and card arrangements using axes, wrapping, gap, and alignment.
**Grid Tracks and Areas** — Build two-dimensional page structure using tracks, auto-placement, and explicit areas when justified.
**Flex or Grid** — Explain why each mechanism fits different content requirements, including source versus visual order.
**Alignment and Min-Content Failures** — Diagnose shrinking, min-content overflow, and unexpected grid/flex item sizing.
**Positioning and Layering** — Use relative, absolute, sticky, and stacking contexts cautiously without obscuring content or focus.
**Long and Sparse Content** — Test layouts with unusually long headings, missing images, short content, and localization-like text growth.

modules.title: Layout with Flow, Flexbox, and Grid

lessons.title: **Content-First Breakpoints** — Derive breakpoints from actual layout failure instead of a device catalog.
**Fluid Dimensions** — Use percentages, rem, flexible tracks, min/max, clamp, and intrinsic sizing appropriately.
**Viewport Media Queries** — Respond to constrained space without requiring one fixed screen resolution.
**Component-Level Adaptation** — Use container queries where supported and provide a usable fallback for unsupported environments.
**No-Horizontal-Scroll Review** — Test narrow viewports and 200% zoom, distinguishing justified exceptions from broken layout.
**Input and Motion Preferences** — Respond to reduced motion and relevant user preferences without removing essential information.
**Responsive Failure Triage** — Record measured layout causes and repairs instead of relying on screenshots alone.
**Accessibility Foundations** — Relate semantic HTML, assistive-technology exposure, and the limitations of visual inspection.
**Keyboard Reachability** — Test links and native controls by tabbing through meaningful focus order with no keyboard trap.
**Focus Visibility** — Provide unmistakable focus indication and prevent sticky content from fully obscuring focused controls.
**Names and Relationships** — Inspect image alternatives, form labels, table relationships, and landmark names.
**Contrast and Resizing** — Check representative text/non-text contrast and text resizing against explicit criteria.
**Native Versus Custom Widgets** — Prefer real anchors, buttons, and controls over inaccessible clickable containers.
**Accessibility Test Limits** — Combine keyboard testing, browser accessibility-tree inspection, and automated checks without claiming certification.
**Accessible Error Repair** — Reproduce and fix a missing label, invisible focus, and invalid-form guidance regression.
**Image Formats and Sources** — Select an appropriate format and local asset sizes without an external hosting dependency.
**Responsive Images** — Use width/size information, srcset and sizes or picture where genuinely beneficial.
**Loading and Layout Stability** — Provide intrinsic dimensions or aspect ratios, inspect waterfalls, and reduce image-caused layout shifts.
**File Organization** — Organize semantic page templates and layered or component-based CSS without importing a UI framework.
**Progressive Enhancement** — Start with usable documents, add supported CSS features, and evaluate fallback when a feature is absent.
**Cross-Browser Differences** — Reproduce one meaningful standards/support difference or a supplied compatibility scenario.
**Regressions and Refactoring** — Refactor repeated styles while proving navigation, layout, and focus behavior did not regress.
**Define the Content Contract** — Choose a concrete multi-page information service, audiences, tasks, constraints, and success criteria.
**Architecture and Navigation** — Plan pages, landmarks, content hierarchy, form purposes, and reusable presentation patterns.
**Incremental Implementation** — Build the static interface using semantic HTML and maintainable styles with meaningful commits.
**Responsive and Keyboard Audit** — Exercise real tasks in narrow/wide viewports, keyboard-only use, zoom, and relevant preference modes.
**Failure Injection** — Introduce broken resource, invalid-control, and overflow scenarios and document their repair.
**Evidence and Reproduction** — Prepare a self-contained clean-checkout project with validation steps and verifiable observations.
**Trade-Off Defense** — Explain semantic, accessibility, cascade, layout, compatibility, and resource decisions with known limitations.

modules.title: Static Site Integration and Technical Review

outcomes.description: Author valid, meaningful HTML documents with appropriate metadata, document structure, headings, landmarks, and semantic elements; explain what the browser constructs from their markup.
Structure navigable content using accurate links, lists, figures, images, and data tables, including suitable text alternatives and understandable relationships.
Create usable native HTML forms with correctly associated labels, input types, field grouping, constraints, accessible error guidance, and an honest explanation of client-side validation limits.
Predict, explain, and debug computed CSS results using selectors, cascade origins, layers, importance, specificity, inheritance, custom properties, and source order.
Apply readable type, color, spacing, box-model geometry, logical properties, and maintainable visual tokens while retaining content readability and user control.
Implement robust document-flow, Flexbox, and Grid layouts, selecting mechanisms according to content and diagnosing overflow, sizing, and alignment failures.
Design interfaces that adapt to viewport and content constraints using fluid dimensions, responsive breakpoints, media and container queries where appropriate, and resilient fallback behavior.
Build and evaluate essential semantic, keyboard, focus, form, contrast, and reduced-motion accessibility behavior, identifying limitations of automated checks.
Select and integrate suitable local media assets with descriptive alternatives, dimensions, responsive image options, and measured loading and layout-stability considerations.

Organize a maintainable HTML/CSS codebase with reusable patterns, low-conflict selectors, progressive enhancement, and defensible cross-browser fallbacks without requiring JavaScript or a CSS framework.
Reproduce, investigate, and correct representative markup, cascade, layout, form, accessibility, and asset-loading failures using browser tools, validation, and documented observations.
Deliver and defend a complete, independently reproducible, multi-page static interface that meets stated content, accessibility, responsiveness, and maintenance constraints.
